claims.claim_text: Walmart accounted for approximately 85% of SYM's total revenue for fiscal year ended September 27, 2025, and a significant majority of the $22.5B backlog. Walmart is implementing Symbotic systems in all of Walmart's 42 regional distribution centers under the 2022 Walmart MAA.
claims.subject: Symbotic Inc.
claims.object_value: Walmart Inc. (~85% of FY25 revenue; 42 regional DCs)
claims.source_quote: Walmart, our largest customer, accounted for approximately 85% of our total revenue in the fiscal year ended September 27, 2025 and for a significant majority of our $22.5 billion backlog as of September 27, 2025. ... we amended and restated our Master Automation Agreement with Walmart in 2022 (2022 Walmart MAA) to implement our Systems in all of Walmart's 42 regional distribution centers

claims.claim_text: In January 2025, Symbotic acquired the Advanced Systems and Robotics (ASR) business from Walmart and signed a 2025 Walmart MAA providing a commitment from Walmart to purchase 400 micro-fulfillment systems (with option for additional 200). Walmart will pay $520M in development funding ($230M at close, $165M at year 1, $125M at year 2).
claims.subject: Symbotic Inc.
claims.object_value: Walmart ASR acquisition + 400-unit micro-fulfillment commitment ($520M dev funding)
claims.source_quote: In January 2025, we acquired the Advanced Systems and Robotics (ASR) business from Walmart and signed a Master Automation Agreement... The 2025 Walmart MAA provides for a commitment, subject to the satisfaction of defined system performance metrics, from Walmart to purchase 400 micro-fulfillment systems, with an option for Walmart to purchase an additional 200... Walmart will pay us a total of $520 million, including $230 million that was paid at the closing of acquisition of ASR, $165 million payable on the first anniversary of the acquisition and $125 million payable on the second anniversary

claims.claim_text: GreenBox Systems LLC is a JV with SoftBank (SYM 35% / SoftBank 65%) with a commercial commitment for at least $7.5 billion in system purchases over a 6-year period. As of September 27, 2025, the GreenBox remaining performance obligation is $11.6 billion, with SYM's maximum exposure to loss of $1,574.2 million and future funding commitments of $1,561.1 million.
claims.subject: Symbotic Inc.
claims.object_value: GreenBox / SoftBank JV: $7.5B 6-year, $11.6B RPO, max exposure $1.57B
claims.source_quote: GreenBox, a strategic joint venture... We own 35% of GreenBox and SoftBank Group owns 65% of GreenBox... the commercial agreement provides for a commitment from GreenBox to expend at least $7.5 billion in the aggregate to purchase our systems over a six-year period... The transaction price allocated to performance obligations that are unsatisfied as of September 27, 2025 was $11.6 billion... maximum exposure to loss of $1,574.2 million while considering its equity investment in the VIE, any amounts owed to the Company for services... and future funding commitments of $1,561.1 million.

claims.claim_text: Symbotic's intellectual property is protected by a portfolio of approximately 1,100 issued and/or pending patents, covering robotics/AI/autonomous mobile robots/vision for warehouse automation.
claims.subject: Symbotic Inc.
claims.source_quote: Our intellectual property is protected by a portfolio of approximately 1,100 issued and/or pending patents.

claims.claim_text: Symbotic reports a material weakness in internal control over financial reporting (timing of cost-of-revenue recognition) as of Sept 27, 2025. Grant Thornton issued an adverse opinion on ICFR. A previously disclosed material weakness on revenue recognition (cost overruns) was remediated in FY2025. Securities class actions (Decker / Traina) allege misstatements re revenue recognition, deployment times, and disclosure controls covering periods Feb 8, 2024 to Feb 5, 2025.
claims.subject: Symbotic Inc.
claims.object_value: Material weakness ICFR (FY25) + adverse Grant Thornton opinion + pending securities class action on rev rec
claims.source_quote: the Company's internal controls over financial reporting were not effective due to the identification of the material weakness... did not effectively design procedures and controls over the timing of the recognition of cost of revenue... Grant Thornton LLP... issued an adverse opinion on the effectiveness of the Company's internal control over financial reporting... the amended complaint asserts claims... on the grounds that the Company made false and/or misleading statements or omissions related to its financial results, deployment times, revenue recognition, and internal controls.

claims.claim_text: C&S Wholesale Grocers is an affiliate / related-party customer of Symbotic. Revenue recognized from C&S was $12.2M in FY25, $58.9M in FY24, $15.8M in FY23. The 10-K discloses the Company shares certain key executives with C&S, an important customer.
claims.subject: Symbotic Inc.
claims.object_value: C&S Wholesale Grocers; FY25 rev $12.2M (down from $58.9M FY24)
claims.source_quote: The Company has customer contracts with C&S relating to System Deployments, software maintenance services and the operations of Systems. Revenue of $12.2 million, $58.9 million, and $15.8 million was recognized for the years ended September 27, 2025, September 28, 2024, and September 30, 2023, respectively, relating to these customer contracts.

claims.claim_text: In Q1 FY2025 Symbotic entered into a commercial agreement with Nueva Wal-Mart de Mexico to implement systems in two locations near Mexico City. Walmart de Mexico is a publicly listed subsidiary of Walmart Inc.
claims.subject: Symbotic Inc.
claims.object_value: Nueva Wal-Mart de Mexico (Walmex) - 2 sites near Mexico City
claims.source_quote: In the first quarter of fiscal year 2025, we entered into a commercial agreement with Nueva Wal Mart de Mexico, S. de R.L. de C.V to implement our systems in two of their locations near Mexico City.
